# About Adside

We believe paid ads can be a profitable, predictable growth channel for startups and brands. We are building Adside to make that true.

## A word from the founders

We are Robin and Guillaume, two French founders in San Francisco. We met through a common friend and worked side by side in the same coworking space for four years. Before Adside, we bootstrapped a software company together and sold it.

At that company we ran our own paid ads on Meta, Google and Reddit. It took trial, error and some expensive mistakes, but we eventually made them profitable. What struck us is how much of that work was mechanical: research, setup, monitoring, resizing, reporting. Exactly the kind of work AI is good at.

Most startups never get that far. Ads have a reputation for being complex, opaque and easy to waste money on, and the reputation is often deserved. Our study of YC companies found that only a small fraction run paid ads at all. We think that it is a huge missed opportunity, and we’re here to help more startups get more clients with paid ads easily.

So we started Adside in early 2026. There is no obvious default for a company that wants to run paid ads, the way Stripe is the default for payments. We want Adside to be it: a platform you can run yourself, or a managed service where we run everything for you.

Curious about the YC numbers? Read our study: What ads are YC companies running?

## We're re-building a paid marketing agency from the ground up using agents for operational work, instead of people

TL;DR: We're building Adside, the AI that manages your ads on Meta, Google and LinkedIn, etc. We’re building the tool we wished we had in our previous company (B2B SaaS PLG) that we sold earlier this year.

👉 YouTube Video

iframe

## What Adside does

  * We help you build your strategy: what to run, and who to target.
  * We make your creatives (getting much better on this very soon) and optimized landing pages (soon too)
  * We run, monitor and improve your campaigns across Meta, Google, LinkedIn, Reddit, Twitter (and more coming)
  * We help you dig, investigate, fix - all autonomously. An AI ad expert working 24/7 on your account.

If you want someone to manage your AI agency, we even offer a managed service where an expert from our network can help you refine your strategy then manage the agents. 

We're live with 30 companies and we’re getting so much inbound via our own ads that we’re now charging $50 per demo. We’re at day 0 and eager to build, so please send your ideas and feedback!

Image: uploaded image

And here are some of the Adside-generated ads we use for our own ads on Meta: https://app.adside.ai/share/g19CkswUgoc84An3FBlrgUld

If you use Adside you’ll get totally different designs, wording and value proposition - it's all personalized to you.

## Why we started this

At our previous company, paid ads became our main channel and we kind of created our own playbook. It worked better than anything else but it was a real pain: accounts, tracking, audiences, creatives, then daily management across multiple platforms that don't talk to each other.

You don't have to be a genius to look at Claude code and then Google Ads manager or talk to any ads agency and understand there's a massive opportunity to improve the current experience. It's actually hard to do it well, and the market opportunity is very deep (and fun). $800Bn is spent on digital advertising every year, an extra $400Bn goes to people who manage this spend - with incumbents like WPP at $18 billion in revenue. That's who we’re going after.

### Who we are

We’re best friends and repeat founders, including one company in marketing automation that we built and sold earlier this year. 

Robin started his first company in 2016 (HireSweet, AI for recruiting - $4M annual revenue), did YC for the first time in the Winter 2020. Then left HireSweet in 2024, started an angel fund that invested in 130+ amazing companies total, including Starcloud, Mastra, Conductor, Blaxel, Casco, Sygaldry, and so many more + launched Botdog with Gui.

Gui has been a software engineer in tech for 13 years (Globality, Staff at Oscar Health, Defacto) and holds master's degrees from CentraleSupélec and Berkeley. He most recently built Botdog together with Rob. You might find him on a surf board at Ocean Beach when the conditions are right.

For an agent to run ads well, it needs more than a company's own numbers. It needs to know what everyone else in the market is running: which formats they use, which ads they've kept live for months. A lot of Adside's customers are Y Combinator and other startups, so understanding how startups advertise is core to the product.

Both of those needs point to the same place: the public ad libraries and Apify.

## Sizing up one competitor meant opening three websites by hand

Meta, Google, and LinkedIn all keep public ad libraries, which is great, except each one is a separate website with its own layout, its own quirks, and no clean export. To see what a single competitor was running, you'd open the Meta Ad Library, then the Google Ads Transparency Center, then the LinkedIn Ad Library, and check three different pages.

Doing that for one brand is tedious. Doing it for a list of 50 competitors is a lost afternoon, and there's still nothing structured at the end of it: no history, no way to compare formats, no way to see which ads have been running for two years (the ones that are quietly working). None of it scales, and none of it is queryable.

> None of these ad libraries have an official API, and maintaining scrapers for three moving targets in-house is a full-time job nobody wanted. With Apify, adding a platform is finding or building one Actor.
> -- Robin Choy, co-founder, Adside

## One company in, every live ad out, across all three platforms

AdsSpy wires the three ad libraries together with Apify Actors. You add a competitor, and the pipeline spreads out across platforms.

For Meta, Adside built and published its own Actors on the Apify platform. Meta Ad Library Page Resolver finds the brand's real Facebook page, which is harder than it sounds: the library has no website field, and a name search returns lookalikes. Meta Ad Library Ads Scraper then pulls the live creatives. For search and display, Google Ads Scraper reads the Transparency Center by domain, which is exact. For B2B, LinkedIn Ad Library Scraper covers the sponsored ads most tools miss.

Everything comes back as clean JSON through the `run-sync-get-dataset-items` endpoint, gets structured with AI, and lands in one dashboard: the ad copy, the format, the landing page, and how long each creative has been live. On top of that, Adside runs social listening with two more Actors.
